adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:73 — Adding a username that is already a member makes group.add hit GroupUser uniqueness (RecordInvalid, 500), and since the loop has no transaction the earlier adds stay saved while the UI gets an error.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff adds a loop `usernames.split(",").each { |username| ... group.add(user) }` followed by `group.save` with no deduplication and no transaction. The diff does not show what `Group#add` does, so the specific claim about `GroupUser` uniqueness raising `RecordInvalid`/500 is not directly verifiable from this PR alone. However, given the new direct `group.add` calls, failing to guard against already-members and not wrapping the batch operation in a transaction is a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case/robustness concern (could error mid-loop and/or leave partial changes depending on `Group#add` implementation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete(user_id) on a has_many :through only deletes the join rows and skips the GroupUser destroy callbacks that Group#remove ran, so user_count is not decremented and primary_group_id/title are not cleared.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff switches membership removal logic to `group.users.delete(user_id)`. For `has_many :through` associations this performs a direct delete of join rows (typically `delete_all`) and does not instantiate/destroy the join model, so any join-model `destroy` callbacks or counter-cache updates that would have happened via the prior `group.remove(user)` path (seen in the removed `update_patch`) will be skipped. This can plausibly leave derived state (e.g., cached counts or cleanup side effects) inconsistent after removal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The public members endpoint does not bound limit/offset, so ?limit=10000000 dumps the whole membership and a negative limit or offset makes Postgres raise (500).

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and passes them directly into `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation or bounds. This allows arbitrarily large `limit` values (potentially dumping/DoS via huge responses) and negative `offset` (e.g., `offset = -1`) which will generate SQL with a negative OFFSET and can raise a Postgres error (500). The finding matches the code introduced in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6 — The public group members page now shows only the first 50 members and has no pagination controls, so larger non-automatic groups can no longer be browsed in full.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always paginate results (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`), whereas previously only automatic groups were limited and non-automatic groups returned all members. On the public members page, the template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` now iterates `{{#each m in members}}`, with `members` populated only by `model.findMembers()` (which uses the default `limit: 50` in `Discourse.Group`), but no pagination UI/controls were added in the public `group/members.hbs` template or route/controller to change `offset`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25 — findMembers builds the URL from the name being edited but not yet saved, so paging or reloading after add/remove in the admin editor while renaming requests the wrong or a missing group.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers()` builds the request URL from `this.get('name')` (`/groups/<name>/members.json`). In the admin group editor template (`admin/templates/group.hbs`), the group `name` is editable via a bound `text-field`, while paging (`next`/`previous`) and post-mutation reloads call `model.findMembers()` (paging actions in `admin-group.js.es6`; `addMembers`/`removeMember` call `findMembers()` after PUT/DELETE). If an admin edits the name but hasn’t saved yet, subsequent paging or reload after add/remove will use the unsaved new name and can request a non-existent/wrong group members endpoint. This behavior is directly introduced/exposed by the new paging and reload-on-mutation flow combined with name-based URL construction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — After removing the last member on the last page, the offset is clamped with the stale user_count and stays past the new total, leaving an empty page.

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.findMembers` the requested `offset` is clamped using the model’s current `user_count`: `offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));`. When `removeMember` runs, it calls `self.findMembers()` immediately after the DELETE, but the model’s `user_count`/`offset` are still the pre-removal values. If you remove the last user on the last page (e.g. `user_count=51, limit=50, offset=50`), the clamp still sends `offset=50`. The server then returns `total=50` with an empty `members` list (offset equals total), and the model is updated to `user_count=50, offset=50`, leaving the UI on an empty last page (`currentPage` remains 2 and `totalPages` computes to 2). Nothing in the diff adjusts the offset down to the last non-empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:58 — addMembers/removeMember have no failure handling and the username input is never cleared, so errors are silently swallowed and clicking Add again re-sends the same usernames (see the duplicate-add 500).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `addMembers` action in `admin-group.js.es6` that calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` but explicitly does not clear the input (`// TODO: should clear the input`) and never resets `usernames` on success. This means clicking “Add” again will resend the same usernames value. Additionally, `Discourse.Group#addMembers` and `#removeMember` in `discourse/models/group.js` only attach a `.then(...)` handler and do not handle rejection locally, so failures from the `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` requests are not surfaced/handled here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Unknown usernames or ones with surrounding whitespace are silently skipped and the call still returns success, so the admin gets no signal that nobody was added.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and does `User.find_by_username(username)` without stripping whitespace. Usernames with surrounding spaces (e.g. " bob ") won’t match and will be skipped, and unknown usernames are also skipped due to the `if user = ...` guard. The action then still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if zero members were added, giving the admin no feedback that nothing happened.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 — The remove_member automatic-group spec uses xhr :put, but the route is DELETE; controller specs don't check the verb, so the test passes while exercising a verb that isn't routed.

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:129 — The remove spec only checks group.users.count, so it passes even though user_count and primary_group_id are left stale, and no spec covers duplicate or unknown usernames.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new membership mutation endpoints (`add_members`, `remove_member`) and corresponding specs. This is a per-username lookup plus per-user membership insert, which will scale poorly for large comma-separated lists (classic N+1/per-item DB work). It’s a performance/efficiency concern introduced by the new bulk-add endpoint, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — group.add persists each GroupUser immediately with no transaction, so a duplicate/already-member username raises mid-loop (500) leaving earlier users added and group.save's result meaningless.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff shows a loop over `usernames.split(",")` calling `group.add(user)` for each found user, then `group.save` afterward. The diff does not show what `Group#add` does, so the claim that each add “persists immediately” and will raise on duplicates (causing a mid-loop 500 with partial membership) is not verifiable from this PR alone. However, it is still a concrete review concern that this endpoint has no transaction/rollback and no explicit handling for duplicate/already-member usernames or mid-loop failures, and the final `group.save` may not meaningfully represent the success of the membership changes depending on how `group.add` is implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:64 — addMembers AJAX has no catch or user feedback (and input is not cleared or disabled), so 422/500 failures are silent and a double-click resubmits already-added users.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` the `addMembers` action just calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` and returns nothing/doesn’t attach a `.catch()` or `.then()` for UI state, and the template button isn’t disabled while the request is in-flight. There’s also an explicit `// TODO: should clear the input`, and the input is never cleared, so repeated clicks can resend the same usernames. However, whether failures are truly “silent” can’t be proven from this diff alone (there may be a global AJAX error handler elsewhere), so it’s best treated as a concrete UX/resiliency gap introduced by the change rather than a strictly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:56 — removeMember promise is fire-and-forget with no error handling, so a failed DELETE gives the admin no feedback after they confirmed removal.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `removeMember` action triggers `self.get("model").removeMember(member);` inside the `bootbox.confirm` callback but does not return/handle the AJAX promise. In `group.js`, `removeMember` returns `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` with no error handling. From the diff, a failed DELETE would not surface any explicit feedback in this action flow (and callers can’t await it), which is a concrete UX/robustness concern, though not provably a functional defect given possible global AJAX error handling outside the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:13 — findMembers moved from awaited afterModel to un-awaited setupController, so there is no loading state and request failures are swallowed, leaving an empty member list with no error.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin_group_route.js`, the `afterModel` hook that returned `model.findMembers()` was removed, and `setupController` now calls `model.findMembers();` without returning/awaiting the promise. Since `findMembers` performs `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)`, a request failure will no longer reject the route transition (no error route/handler via the hook chain) and the template will render with `members` unset/empty, with the rejection potentially becoming unhandled. This is a behavior regression compared to the previous awaited `afterModel` implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 — Public group members fetch is now fire-and-forget without error handling, so a failed request silently renders an empty table instead of routing to the error state.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`, the previous implementation returned `model.findMembers()` from `afterModel`, so an AJAX failure would reject the route's model hook chain and trigger Ember's error handling (error substates). The new code calls `model.findMembers();` inside `setupController` without returning/awaiting the promise, so a failed `/groups/:name/members.json` request will not transition to an error state. Combined with the template change to iterate `{{#each m in members}}` (where `members` is only set on success in `Group#findMembers`), the UI will render no rows (empty table) rather than entering an error route/state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:31 — findMembers blindly applies whichever response arrives last, so rapid next/previous clicks can render an out-of-order page and reset offset to a stale value.

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, each AJAX response unconditionally calls `self.setProperties({ user_count: result.meta.total, limit: result.meta.limit, offset: result.meta.offset, members: ... })`. The admin controller actions `next`/`previous` update `group.offset` and then immediately call `group.findMembers()` again. With rapid paging clicks, multiple `/groups/:name/members.json` requests can be in flight; because there is no cancellation or request sequencing, an earlier request can resolve after a later one and overwrite `members` and `offset` with stale `result.meta.offset`, rendering the wrong page and resetting the offset backward.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit/offset are unvalidated, so negative values cause a Postgres LIMIT/OFFSET error (500), limit=0 yields division-by-zero paging on the client, and huge limits allow unbounded queries.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces direct use of request params without validation: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. This allows `offset < 0` to be passed through (which can raise a DB error and produce a 500), allows `limit = 0` to be returned in `meta.limit` and persisted into the client model (`self.setProperties({ limit: result.meta.limit, ... })`), which then feeds `totalPages`/`currentPage` computations that divide by `limit`, and allows arbitrarily large `limit` values leading to potentially unbounded/heavy queries. The issue is grounded in the newly added paging/meta behavior in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Default limit of 50 now truncates non-automatic groups on the public members page, which has no pagination controls, so members beyond 50 silently disappear.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit`/`offset` with a default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` for *all* groups (removing the previous `if group.automatic?` guard). On the client side, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now calls `model.findMembers()`, and `discourse/models/group.js#findMembers` requests `/groups/:name/members.json` with that limit/offset and stores only `members` for the current page. The public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` simply iterates `{{#each m in members}}` and this diff does not add any pagination controls there, so only the first 50 members will be displayed and the rest are inaccessible from this page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — After removing the last member on the final page, the reload keeps the stale offset and shows an empty page with currentPage > totalPages and inconsistent next/previous state.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `removeMember` triggers `self.findMembers()` after deletion but does not adjust `offset`. `findMembers` computes the request offset from the *current* `this.get("user_count")` before the reload (`var offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`), which is stale immediately after removing a user. If you delete the last member on the last page (e.g., `user_count` was 51, `limit` 50, `offset` 50), the reload requests `offset=50` even though the new total is 50, so `GroupsController#members` returns an empty `members` array. This leaves the UI on an empty page and `currentPage/totalPages` can become inconsistent (also amplified by `totalPages` using `Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1`, which overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:58 — The reload findMembers() in addMembers/removeMember is not returned from then(), so its failure is unhandled and the outer promise resolves before the list is refreshed.
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that findMembers() is now asynchronous and not properly chained/handled, leading to unhandled failures and the surrounding logic (controller/outer promise) continuing before member data has refreshed, i.e., a race condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete on a has_many :through deletes join rows without running GroupUser destroy callbacks (unlike the old group.remove), and returns success even when the user was not a member.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `render json: success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. Using `delete` on an association removes join rows without instantiating/destroying join models, so any join-model `destroy` callbacks would be skipped (unlike the previous code path which called `group.remove(user)` in `update_patch`). Also, if the given `user_id` was not a member, `group.users.delete(user_id)` is a no-op and the action can still return success. This is a real behavior/semantics change, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it breaks correctness in this app (callbacks/expected error behavior aren’t shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:72 — Unknown or whitespace-padded usernames are silently skipped while the endpoint returns success, so the admin gets no signal that some additions failed.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users found by `User.find_by_username(username)`. It does not `strip` each `username`, so whitespace-padded entries (e.g. " bob") won’t match and will be skipped. Nonexistent usernames are also skipped. Regardless, the action renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, giving the admin no indication that some requested additions did not occur. This behavior is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — usernames.split assumes a String, so an array-form usernames[] param raises NoMethodError (500) instead of a 400.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff sets `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. If the request submits `usernames[]` (an array), Rails will provide an Array, which does not respond to `split`, causing a `NoMethodError` (500) rather than a handled client error. This behavior is directly visible in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Public members endpoint accepts an unbounded user-controlled limit (no max clamp), letting anonymous callers pull an entire large group in one request and load the DB.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and applies it directly to the query (`group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`) without any maximum clamp. Since this is the public `groups_controller` endpoint (not admin) and `find_group` only checks `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`, a caller who can view the group can request an arbitrarily large `limit`, potentially forcing large DB work and response sizes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — Negative limit/offset values go straight into SQL LIMIT/OFFSET, so PostgreSQL raises and the public endpoint returns a 500 (now reachable for every group, not only automatic ones).

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff now does `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then applies them directly: `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamping/validation to prevent negative values. A request like `?offset=-1` will generate a negative SQL OFFSET, which PostgreSQL rejects and would surface as a 500 on this public endpoint. This pagination previously only applied to automatic groups, but the diff makes it apply to all groups, increasing reachability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of Group#remove, which skips GroupUser callbacks and cleanup (e.g. primary_group_id), so a removed user can keep group-derived attributes.

This bypasses whatever custom logic `Group#remove` encapsulates (the diff itself shows such a method existed/was used), making it a behavioral change in how removals are performed. If `Group#remove` performs cleanup beyond deleting the association, that cleanup will no longer run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:53 — Username and group name are put into the bootbox.confirm HTML message without escaping; only safe while username/group-name validators block HTML characters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 — "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues `xhr :put` against a DELETE-only route, so the spec does not exercise the real HTTP contract and only passes because controller specs skip routing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:94 — Automatic-group 422 specs hardcode `group_id: 1`, which relies on a seeded automatic group; if it's missing, Group.find raises and the specs fail or pass for the wrong reason instead of using `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds specs that assert 422 behavior for automatic groups by hardcoding `group_id: 1` (and similarly in remove_member) instead of creating an automatic group in the test. In this diff, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` and `#remove_member` both call `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)` before checking `group.automatic`, so if id 1 is not present in the test DB the controller will raise and the spec will fail (or, if some seeded group with id 1 exists, the test is coupled to seed state rather than the intended setup). This is a concrete, diff-grounded brittleness/incorrect test setup issue, but it affects test reliability rather than production behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:52 — Update spec edits seeded group id 1 without asserting it is automatic, and the removed rename assertion for non-automatic groups (`name.should == 'fred'`) has no replacement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:112 — Deleted "succeeds silently when removing non-members" coverage is not replaced; removing a non-member or unknown user_id via `group.users.delete(user_id)` is untested and likely raises RecordNotFound.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the prior spec case that covered deleting a non-member (“succeeds silently when removing non-members”) and replaces membership removal with a new `remove_member` endpoint that calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` (Admin::GroupsController#remove_member). adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:91 — Deleted "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users" coverage is not replaced; add_members has no tests for unknown usernames, users who are already members, or a missing usernames param.

In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are iterated and unknown usernames are silently skipped (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`), and `params.require(:usernames)` will raise if missing. The updated specs only cover adding valid users and blocking automatic groups, with no replacement tests for (a) unknown usernames being ignored, (b) usernames that are already members, or (c) missing `usernames` param behavior. This is a specific, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19 — Public GroupsController#members changes its response shape to {members, meta} and adds pagination for all groups, but the diff adds or updates no spec for it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to return a new JSON shape `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and to paginate for all groups (see `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb` where it now computes `total = group.users.count`, applies `limit/offset`, and `render json:` with `members` and `meta`). In the same diff, only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` is updated/expanded; there is no added or modified spec covering `GroupsController#members` or its new response contract/pagination behavior. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly introduced nontrivial behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Untested edge cases: limit and offset are unbounded, so negative, zero, or very large values pass straight to SQL (a negative LIMIT/OFFSET errors in Postgres) and no spec covers them.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed directly into `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. Since `.to_i` will produce negative integers for inputs like "-5", this can generate SQL with a negative OFFSET (and possibly LIMIT), which can error at the DB layer and return a 500. The diff also adds no spec coverage for these edge cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — Pagination math has no JS tests and totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (50/50 gives 2 pages), so "next" loads an empty page.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50/50 => 2 pages). With `currentPage` based on `offset/limit + 1`, clicking `next` from offset 0 sets `offset` to `Math.min(0+limit, user_count)` => 50, and `findMembers()` requests `offset=50`, yielding an empty member list for a 50-user group. This matches the finding’s “next loads an empty page” behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — New Group model methods (findMembers meta handling, addMembers, removeMember) and the changed return value of findMembers have no QUnit coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds/changes substantial client-side logic in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js` (`findMembers` now fetches `/members.json` and mutates `user_count/limit/offset/members`, and new `addMembers`/`removeMember` methods perform PUT/DELETE and then reload via `findMembers`). The PR updates routes/controllers/templates to rely on these side effects (e.g., `model.findMembers();` without `.then(...)`). However, this diff adds no corresponding JavaScript/QUnit tests for the new behaviors or the changed `findMembers` semantics, while only Ruby controller specs were updated/added. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded test-coverage gap rather than a proven functional bug.
